title: Tips for Big-O Analysis?
content: I'm having trouble determining whether nested loops always mean O(n^2). Does anyone have a systematic approach for analyzing complexity?

replies.content: Not always! If the inner loop runs a constant number of times, it's still O(n). Look at how many times the inner loop body actually executes total.
Great question Alice. I recommend the 'counting method' - count the total number of operations as a function of n. We'll cover this more in Wednesday's lecture.
I found it helpful to trace through small examples (n=1,2,3,4) and look for the pattern.

title: JOIN vs Subquery Performance
content: When should we use JOINs versus subqueries? Are there performance differences in practice?

replies.content: In general, JOINs are optimized better by most RDBMS query planners. However, correlated subqueries can sometimes be more readable. We'll benchmark this in the lab next week.
I tested both on the sample database and JOINs were consistently faster for our dataset sizes.

title: Intuition for Eigenvalues
content: Can someone explain eigenvalues intuitively? I can compute them but I don't really understand what they mean geometrically.

replies.content: Think of a matrix as a transformation. Eigenvectors are directions that don't change direction under the transformation - they only get scaled. The eigenvalue is the scaling factor. I'll bring a visual demo to class.
3Blue1Brown has an amazing video on this! Search 'Essence of Linear Algebra' on YouTube.

title: Double Integral Bounds
content: I keep getting the bounds wrong when converting from rectangular to polar coordinates for double integrals. Any tips?

replies.content: Draw the region first! Then figure out the range of r and theta by tracing the boundary. It really helps to sketch it.

title: Green's Theorem Applications
content: Can Green's theorem be applied to any closed curve, or does the region need to be simply connected?

replies.content: The standard form requires a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth curve bounding a simply connected region. For multiply-connected regions, you can modify the theorem by introducing cuts.

title: Choosing Learning Rate
content: How do you pick a good learning rate for gradient descent? My linear regression keeps diverging or converging too slowly.

replies.content: Try starting with 0.01 and adjusting by factors of 10. You can also implement a learning rate schedule that decreases over time. We'll cover adaptive methods like Adam next month.
Feature scaling/normalization also helps a lot. If your features have very different ranges, gradient descent struggles.

title: Understanding Recursion
content: I understand loops but recursion is confusing me. Can someone explain when to use recursion vs iteration?

replies.content: Recursion is natural for problems that have a recursive structure - like tree traversal, factorial, Fibonacci. If you can break a problem into smaller identical subproblems, recursion is a good fit.
I found it helpful to trace through the call stack on paper. Start with the base case and work up.
